motions.purpose: Draw-in of chart elements when the chart enters view: lines trace, bars grow from the baseline, markers pop, bands and labels fade in with a short stagger.
motions.model: Solid observed lines animate stroke-dashoffset over their measured length; dashed epistemic styles fade instead (dash pattern must not be corrupted); bars scaleY from the y=0 baseline; stagger is capped at 900 ms.
motions.limitations: Purely presentational; encodes no data meaning. Order of appearance follows document order, not value order.
motions.reducedMotion: All elements render in their final state immediately.
motions.accessibility: The SVG carries role=img with an aria-label from the chart title; data is also available as text in captions per the chart rules.

motions.purpose: Violin (distribution) plots grow horizontally from their centerline on reveal (scaleX 0-1, ~90 ms stagger per violin), then quartile box, 5-95 whiskers and the median dot fade/pop in.
motions.model: Shape is a Gaussian-kernel KDE with Silverman bandwidth h = 0.9 * min(sigma, IQR/1.34) * n^(-1/5), evaluated at 48 evenly spaced points over [min-h, max+h]; quartiles/percentiles use linear interpolation (R-7). Fully deterministic, no randomness.
motions.limitations: Widths are normalized per violin (each scaled to its own max density): widths are NOT comparable across violins, only shapes and positions are. The KDE smooths h beyond the observed range, so tails extend slightly past the data. The grow animation itself is presentational; only the final shape is the analytic claim.
motions.reducedMotion: Final state immediately (no growth, no stagger).
motions.accessibility: SVG carries role=img with an aria-label; category names render as axis text; summary statistics (median, quartiles) are visible as static marks.

motions.purpose: chart.morphTo(patch) glides existing scatter points (matched by index) to their new positions, fades removed points out and pops added points in; bars glide via height scaling; lines crossfade over 300 ms because a path 'd' cannot tween.
motions.model: Pure playback of two caller-supplied datasets; no interpolation model beyond the visual easing between start and end positions.
motions.limitations: Axes do NOT rescale during a morph - fix the domain via x/y min/max or accept points moving off-plot. Index-based matching asserts identity: if point i in the old and new datasets is not the same entity, the glide fabricates a continuity that is not in the data. Intermediate positions during the glide carry no data meaning.
motions.reducedMotion: New data applied instantly; the returned promise resolves immediately.
motions.exportState: New data applied instantly, no transitions.
motions.accessibility: End states are complete static charts; the transition adds no information, so nothing is lost by skipping it.

motions.purpose: Presenter-triggered ONE-SHOT attention sweep (chart.sheen(i)): a short bright segment travels once along a line path and fades (~900 ms WAAPI); scatter points emit one expanding ring each (20 ms stagger); violins get a single outline brightness pulse. The overlay node is removed when the animation ends.
motions.model: None - decorative-adjacent focus cue that encodes no data. It is legitimate only because it is presenter-driven, single-shot and self-removing; use at most once per claim.
motions.limitations: Honest caveat: this is the closest the system comes to decoration. It must never loop, never persist a glow/drop-shadow, and must not substitute for an annotation or reference line when the emphasis IS the claim.
motions.reducedMotion: No-op: the call returns without rendering anything.
motions.exportState: No-op: nothing is rendered in export mode.
motions.accessibility: Carries no information, so its absence (reduced motion, export) loses nothing; the presenter's spoken claim plus static labels remain the record.

motions.purpose: Orchestrated scene entrance (chart.enter()): axis lines sweep in via stroke-dash trace, gridlines fade in bottom-to-top in sequence, ticks cascade (y slides from the left, x drops from above), THEN the data layer enters per chart type on a single deterministic timeline (cubic-bezier easings only, no randomness). Replayable; seek01(t) renders any instant synchronously for headless verification (?demo=<type>&t=).
motions.model: A track-based timeline: each element gets {t0, duration, easing, apply(p)}; apply() is idempotent so any time point can be rendered directly without playing through. Spring overshoots use an analytic back-out ease.
motions.limitations: Purely presentational ordering; the sequence encodes reading order (frame before data), not data meaning. Bar spring overshoot briefly exceeds the true height by ~6% before settling; value labels only appear after the bar has settled at the true value.
motions.reducedMotion: enter() renders the final frame immediately (enterFinal), including bar value labels at their true values.
motions.exportState: Final frame immediately; no transitions, no transient nodes.
motions.accessibility: SVG carries role=img with an aria-label; the finished chart is identical whether or not the entrance played.

motions.purpose: During the line entrance the path draws tip-first with a comet head (pen-like dot) and a flowing tabular-numeral readout beside it; markers pop exactly when the comet passes them (arc-length solved per marker); when the line settles the comet fades, the gradient area fills in one left-to-right sweep and the uncertainty band inflates outward from its centerline in a single breath.
motions.model: The readout reports the y-value of the DRAWN monotone (Fritsch-Carlson) curve at the pen tip's current x, obtained by inverting the y-scale at getPointAtLength; at completion it equals the final data point exactly. Marker pop times invert the draw easing so visual pass and pop coincide.
motions.limitations: Between samples the readout shows the monotone interpolation of the plotted curve, not a measured value - it can never contradict the curve because it IS the curve. Dashed epistemic lines are revealed by clip sweep instead (no comet, no readout - a projection must not be read like an observation) so the dash pattern is never corrupted. The band's one-shot breath overshoots its final width by about 5% for a few frames; it settles to the exact interval and never loops.
motions.reducedMotion: Final frame; comet and readout are never created.
motions.exportState: Final frame; comet and readout are never created.
motions.accessibility: The readout is transient and redundant with the plotted curve; the persistent record is the curve, markers, direct labels and caption.

motions.purpose: Bar entrance: each bar springs from the baseline with a slight overshoot, then its value label counts up from 0 to the true value in tabular numerals and PERSISTS as a static label.
motions.model: Label text is fmt(value * easedProgress); at progress 1 it renders the exact caller-supplied value with the standard formatter.
motions.limitations: Intermediate count values are presentational (monotone ramp toward the truth), not data. The spring overshoot briefly exceeds the true bar height by ~6%; the label only becomes visible after the overshoot resolves.
motions.reducedMotion: Labels render immediately at their final values.
motions.exportState: Labels render immediately at their final values.
motions.accessibility: Final labels are static text in the SVG; nothing is conveyed only by the count.

motions.purpose: Presenter-triggered emphasis: chart.vurgula(i) gives the target bar ONE scale pulse (~6%, 440 ms, never repeated) while every other bar dims to 30%, and an assertion callout slides in beside the target; chart.kumeVurgula(mask) does the same for a scatter subset (one small pop per selected point, non-selected dim to 22%). vurgula(null) restores everything.
motions.model: None - a focus state plus a single one-shot cue. Dimming is a persistent comparison state (same law as hover dimming); the pulse is the only transient and self-terminates.
motions.limitations: Dimming hides nothing (siblings stay visible at reduced ink). The pulse must be used at most once per claim; if the emphasis IS the claim, add an annotation or reference line instead. No glow, no filter, nothing persists beyond the dim state and the callout text.
motions.reducedMotion: Dim state and callout apply instantly; no pulse is played.
motions.exportState: Dim state and callout apply instantly (a deliberate comparison state that survives export); no pulse.
motions.accessibility: The callout is real SVG text; the dimmed elements remain readable at 22-30% opacity.

motions.purpose: chart.setData(patch) FLIP transition: index-matched elements glide old-to-new, removed elements fade, added elements pop in; if the domain is not pinned the AXES RESCALE - tick numbers slide odometer-style to their re-numbered positions while grid, series, reference lines and annotations flow together under the interpolated domain. After settling, a short-lived unit-bearing delta chip (e.g. +1,48 px) floats beside each changed element and fades; the engine removes chip nodes afterwards.
motions.model: Per frame the domain and matched data values are linearly interpolated between the two real states and the geometry is fully re-laid-out; delta chips show the exact new-minus-old difference computed from the caller's data, formatted with the y-axis unit.
motions.limitations: Intermediate frames interpolate between two real states and carry no data meaning; the two endpoints are complete honest charts. Index matching asserts identity across datasets - if old i and new i are not the same entity, the glide fabricates continuity. At most 6 chips per update (largest absolute deltas) to avoid chip confetti. Violin setData is not supported.
motions.reducedMotion: New data, new axes and final layout apply instantly; no chips are shown; the promise resolves immediately.
motions.exportState: New data applied instantly; no chips, no transitions.
motions.accessibility: End states are complete static charts; chips are transient and redundant with the visible value change (bar labels update to the new true values).

motions.purpose: Narrative mode: chart.sahnele([{vurgula|kumeVurgula|setData|sheen, not}, ...]) returns {ileri, geri, git} so a deck can bind chart storytelling to its arrow keys; each step applies an emphasis state plus an assertion callout. The engine adds NO global key listeners.
motions.model: Steps are declarative states; setData steps snapshot the prior data so geri() restores it via the same honest transition.
motions.limitations: Composes only motions already declared here (vurgula, kumeVurgula, setData, sheen); it introduces no new visual grammar. Steps should be advanced one at a time - jumping many steps at once plays transitions back-to-back.
motions.reducedMotion: Each step's state applies instantly (dim + callout, data swap without glide).
motions.exportState: The current step's state renders statically; callout text persists as part of the exported frame.
motions.accessibility: Step callouts are real SVG text; every step is a complete readable chart state.
